recommendations.source:
The [pinned package metadata](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/1.1.407/packages/pyright/package.json)
and [CLI reference](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright/blob/main/docs/command-line.md)
describe installation requirements and invocation. This minimal file has no
third-party imports. For a real project, set the intended interpreter, platform,
dependencies, and stubs before interpreting missing-import diagnostics.

## Start with the project environment

Use the documented CLI installation and point Pyright at a small package. Configure the intended Python interpreter, target version, and import paths before interpreting missing-import or unknown-type messages. Choose a diagnostic mode deliberately and review its defaults.

recommendations.reason: Consolidates repeated project-environment advice into one paragraph, preserving every named setting and both reference links.

limitations: No product changes, build, browser pass, or new technical validation is part of this language review.

coverage.method: Read narrative text and prose metadata across the full catalog, then checked for repeated author commentary, vague benefits, and wordy phrasing. Code blocks and source lists were retained unchanged. Long technical qualifiers were preserved when they define scope or interpretation.

validation: Every source string matches exactly once in its stated file.
Every replacement preserves the source snippet's Markdown link targets and inline code spans.
All suggested replacement text is ASCII.
No commands, license declarations, version pins, execution outcomes, or code blocks are changed by the recommendations.
coordinator_consistency_fix: The broader Semgrep Code local/CI host sentence was flagged to the coordinator as a technical consistency observation outside these wording recommendations. The coordinator updated it; the updated host sentence was reread before this file digest was captured. Separate technical provenance remains with the coordinator.

applied_verification.method: Each exact replacement is present once and its original source is absent, comparing text with normalized line endings. Reversing the replacement restores the original reviewed digest directly for Psalm and after CRLF-to-LF normalization for the other 14 files. This verifies that no other text changed. Rechecked source/replacement meaning, Markdown link targets, and inline code spans.
applied_verification.result: All 15 recommendations landed and retain their intended meaning. Scope limits, licenses, version pins, execution status, outputs, and evidence links remain intact.
applied_verification.line_ending_note: The current affected files use CRLF. Fourteen original reviewed files used LF; Psalm already used CRLF. This does not change the wording verification.
